objective: Find a distinct-index sum pair under a deterministic earliest-completed/earliest-left policy in linear time.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: One-pass complement Maps remain current algorithm foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Finding matching entries with retained indices is practical lookup work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Duplicate policies, safe numeric domains and nonmutation transfer to other matching algorithms.

relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Different valid boards chose different pairs when several answers existed.

defects: The brief did not define which pair wins beyond smaller index first.
Junior scanned left-first, disagreeing with right-first Map completion and exceeding the linear goal.
No source/result-ownership checks distinguished consuming or cached outputs.
rationale: Define smallest right index, then smallest left index, and make the policy visible with two new examples. Reference/senior retain each first value index; junior now scans right once with a first-index Map, agreeing on both correctness and O(n). Preserve lookup-before-store so an index is never reused. Three hidden assertions inspect duplicate/right-index tie breaking, signed zero/bounds, frozen and mutable input preservation, fresh mutable pair/empty results and1000 values. An independently written first-index Map solution remains accepted; the old overwriting reference is the baseline wrong program. Bound integer values/target so sum/complement arithmetic is exact; do not invent floating equality rules. No TypeScript cases apply.

objective: Group exact code-point anagrams with stable group/item order and independent output arrays.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Map grouping and canonical text keys remain current algorithm patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Grouping equivalent text by an exact signature is practical data work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Unicode domains, key reuse and avoiding accumulated copies transfer to other aggregators.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Explicit well-formed bounded words keep the sorting-signature exercise manageable.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: UTF-16 halves can merge different words, and repeated group copying makes repeated-word inputs quadratic.

defects: Junior split words into UTF-16 units while other boards iterated code points.
Senior recalculated the same sorted key twice and copied its growing group per word.
Input preservation, fresh nested results and normalization policy were implicit.
A source-reversing implementation passed all old result-only cases.
rationale: Define well-formed Unicode strings and exact iterated code points, excluding normalization/case folding and isolated-surrogate signature ambiguity. Change junior to Array.from; rewrite senior reduce to compute one key and push into the owned group, avoiding quadratic accumulated copies. Three new runtime assertions inspect differently paired surrogate units as distinct code-point words, true supplementary anagrams, combining-mark distinctions, stable text groups, actual mutable/frozen input preservation, independent outer/groups and1000 repeated100-unit words. A Map-of-code-point-frequencies signature is accepted as an independent alternative. Preserve the authored O(n · k log k) comparison-sort target, with n/k lower bounds for empty/short inputs and conservative O(n · k) storage. No TypeScript assertions apply.
